units.text: INT. PUPPET THEATRE - STAGE - NIGHT
Velvet curtains drawn back.
Painted backdrops of a village.
A hundred marionettes hang on rails above the stage like a gallows crowd.
Dust motes in the work lights.
DETECTIVE PRUDENCE ACHEBE (40s, long coat, wry mouth) walks the boards, boots echoing.
VASILI (70s, the puppeteer, hands knotted by arthritis) sits in a high chair at the lip of the stage.
CELESTE (30s, costume designer, thread around her wrist) waits in the front row.
JUDD (50s, theatre manager, blazer, sweat on his lip) hovers near the exit.
OLD BEATRIX (80s, ticket-taker, cardigan, pearl necklace) knits in the aisle seat.
A marionette with a painted gentleman's face hangs center stage, its strings tied in a noose around a hook.
Beneath it, on the boards, a chalk outline of a body.
Everyone comfortable? Good. I'll be brief.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: That's not usual for the police.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: I'm told it's not usual for a puppeteer to be found dead beneath his own puppet either.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Celeste flinches.
Beatrix's needles never stop.
Ms. Celeste, you sewed the costume.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Yes.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Whose idea was the red thread in the collar?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: It was in the sketches.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Whose sketches?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Judd's.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Judd's jaw tightens.
He shifts toward the exit.
Achebe doesn't look at him.
Mr. Judd. Sit down, please.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: I'm fine here.
units.name: JUDD

units.text: You're not. Beatrix, would you tell him where to sit?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Judd, dear. Do as the lady says.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Judd sits.
Slowly.
Vasili's fingers drum the arm of his chair.
Mr. Vasili, you've been quiet.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: I'm old. Quiet is my right.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: You've been here forty years. The dead man was your partner.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Thirty-eight. And he was not my partner. He was my rival.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: Rival for what?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: For the audience. For the last good company in this city.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: And now he's dead, and the company is yours.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Yes.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: Achebe nods.
She walks to the marionette, lifts its limp wooden hand, turns it over.
A tiny brass key is wedged between the fingers.
The key to the box office safe.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Judd's breath hitches.
Mr. Judd, you told my sergeant the safe was untouched.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: It was.
units.name: JUDD

units.text: Then why does the puppet have the key?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Because Vasili put it there.
units.name: JUDD

units.text: I would never.
units.name: VASILI

units.text: He's lying!
units.name: JUDD

units.text: Beatrix. Who handed the dead man his last cup of tea?
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: The needles stop.
For the first time Beatrix looks up.
Her eyes, clouded, rest on Achebe.
I did, dear.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Oh, Beatrix.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Don't fuss. He'd been stealing from the till for years. Poor Judd took the blame, and he's such a nervous boy. I just wanted it to stop.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: Judd stares at her, mouth open.
Achebe sets the marionette's hand down.
Judd.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Yes?
units.name: JUDD

units.text: You're free to go.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Judd bolts.
The door slams.
Celeste pulls the thread from her wrist and stares at it.
Vasili lowers his head.
Mrs. Beatrix. I'll need you to come with me.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Of course, dear. Let me finish the row.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: She knits three more stitches.
Then she folds the work into her lap, stands, and offers Achebe her arm.
Thank you.
units.name: ACHEBE

units.text: Don't thank me. Take care of the little ones.
units.name: BEATRIX

units.text: She nods at the hanging marionettes.
As the two women walk up the aisle, the work lights dim one by one.
The puppets sway on their strings.
